claim: The Ganga rises in the Gangotri glaciers in the Himalaya at about 7,010 m and flows about 2,525 km to the Bay of Bengal (CWC).

evidence.quote: from the Gangotri glaciers in the Himalayas at an elevation of about 7,010m
flows for a total length of about 2,525 km up to its outfall into the Bay of Bengal

notes: CWC's own figures; India-WRIS gives the same 2,525 km (opened, not cited, lite rule).

claim: CWC: Varanasi is on the LEFT bank of the Ganga, about 195 km downstream of Allahabad (Prayagraj).

evidence.quote: The holy city of Varanasi is situated on the left bank of
Ganga about 195 km downstream of Allahabad

notes: Left bank = the bank on your left when you face downstream.

claim: The Varanasi district administration says the city is on the WEST bank of the Ganga.

evidence.quote: Varanasi is a holy town situated on the west bank of the River Ganga

claim: Put together, C02 and C03 mean the river flows northward past the city: only a north-flowing river has its west bank on its left. The Himalaya lie to the north of the basin.

evidence.quote: situated on the left bank of
situated on the west bank of the River Ganga
bounded on the north by the Himalayas
vertices 461-467: 14.8 km

notes: Two government owners plus our geometry agree. Neither page says 'flows north' in words.

claim: Our measurement: past Varanasi the Ganga runs within 45 degrees of north for about 15 km (14.8 km of the Natural Earth line), overall bearing 15 degrees (north by north-east), from 25.211 N 83.008 E to 25.323 N 83.042 E.

evidence.quote: situated on the west bank of the River Ganga

notes: 1:10m line; label 'our measurement, approx.'. Within the stretch the river first heads NNW (bearings 355, 337, 324) then NE (43).

claim: Our measurement: over a 58 km run around Varanasi in which the river never turns south, it ends 37 km further north than it began (overall bearing 31 degrees, north-east).

evidence.locator: method output, run through Varanasi vertex
evidence.quote: river length along line: 58.0 km; straight start-end: 42.7 km; overall bearing 31 deg; northward gain 36.7 km

notes: Run = NE vertices 460-480 (25.205 N 82.996 E to 25.535 N 83.213 E), lat increasing at every vertex. Approximate.

claim: The belief is right for the river as a whole: source-to-delta the Natural Earth line bears 128 degrees (south-east); CWC says that after the Gomti joins below Varanasi the Ganga flows in almost an eastern direction.

evidence.quote: overall bearing first->last vertex 128 deg
Thereafter, the Ganga flows in almost eastern direction

notes: The northward stretch is a local bend, not a reversal of the river.

claim: Allahabad to Varanasi is 117 km in a straight line (our measurement) but about 195 km by river (CWC).

evidence.quote: Allahabad->Varanasi straight: 117 km, bearing 97
about 195 km downstream of Allahabad

notes: Two different bases (straight line vs river length); say both, never subtract as 'wasted' distance.

claim: Our measurement: about a quarter (26%) of the Natural Earth Ganga line has some northward component, so northward bends are not unique to Varanasi.

evidence.quote: length with any northward component 556 km (26%)

notes: Generalised line; use only to avoid 'the only place'.

Hindus believe that one who is graced to die on the land of Varanasi would attain salvation
